h1: What are the zoning setbacks in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Zoning Setbacks: Front, Side and Rear by District
description: Newton's minimum front, side and rear setbacks for SR and MR districts from Ord. Sec. 3.1.3 and 3.2.3, including the December 7, 1953 lot-date split.
short_answer: Newton setbacks depend on your district and on whether your lot was created before or after December 7, 1953. For newer lots, the front, side and rear setbacks are 40, 20 and 25 feet in SR1, 30, 15 and 15 feet in SR2, and 30, 10 and 15 feet in SR3 (Ord. Sec. 3.1.3).

facts.text: Lots created on or after December 7, 1953: front SR1 40', SR2 30', SR3 30'; side SR1 20', SR2 15', SR3 10'; rear SR1 25', SR2 15', SR3 15'.
Lots created before December 7, 1953: front 25' in all SR districts; side SR1 12.5', SR2 7.5', SR3 7.5'; rear SR1 25', SR2 15', SR3 15'.
Lots created on or after December 7, 1953: front MR1 30', MR2 25', MR3 15', MR4 15'; side MR1 10', MR2 10', MR3 7.5', MR4 10'; rear 15' in all MR districts.
Lots created before December 7, 1953: front MR1 25', MR2 25', MR3 15'; side 7.5' in MR1–MR3; rear 15' in MR1–MR3. The table gives no MR4 values for these older lots.
Averaging applies only to the front setback, and no part of a residential building may be closer than 10 feet to the street line (Sec. 1.5.3.B).

qa.q: What is the side setback in SR2?
qa.a: 15 feet for lots created on or after December 7, 1953, and 7.5 feet for older lots (Sec. 3.1.3).

qa.q: Why does the lot creation date matter?
qa.a: Sec. 3.1.3 and 3.2.3 give different setbacks for lots created before December 7, 1953.

qa.q: Can front setback averaging reduce my front setback?
qa.a: Averaging applies only to the front setback, and no part of a residential building may be closer than 10 feet to the street line (Sec. 1.5.3.B).

qa.q: What is the rear setback in SR1?
qa.a: 25 feet for lots of either date (Sec. 3.1.3).
